original_value: Crohn’s disease is among the chronic inflammatory bowel diseases that impact the gastrointestinal tract. Understanding and predicting the severity of inflammation in real-time settings is critical to disease management. Extant literature has primarily focused on studies that are conducted in clinical trial settings to investigate the impact of a drug treatment on the remission status of the disease. This research proposes an analytics methodology where three different types of prediction models are developed to predict and to explain the severity of inflammation in patients diagnosed with Crohn’s disease. The results show that machine-learning-based analytic methods such as gradient boosting machines can predict the inflammation severity with a very high accuracy (area under the curve = 92.82%), followed by regularized regression and logistic regression. According to the findings, a combination of baseline laboratory parameters, patient demographic characteristics, and disease location are among the strongest predictors of inflammation severity in Crohn’s disease patients.

result.paraphrase: Crohn’s disease is one of the chronic inflammatory bowel diseases affecting the gastrointestinal tract. Accurately understanding and forecasting inflammation severity in real time is essential for managing the disease. Previous research has mainly centered on clinical trial settings to examine how drug treatment affects disease remission status. This study presents an analytics approach that develops three distinct prediction model types to predict and explain inflammation severity in patients diagnosed with Crohn’s disease. The findings indicate that machine-learning-based methods, such as gradient boosting machines, achieve very high accuracy in predicting inflammation severity (area under the curve = 92.82%), followed by regularized regression and logistic regression. The results also show that baseline laboratory parameters, patient demographic characteristics, and disease location are among the strongest predictors of inflammation severity in Crohn’s disease patients.
